clue.text: Criminal to John's rear is old con

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters of the following words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook sneaks up behind John while an old prison inmate looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun, the subject of the sentence, but it is the anagram signal, and 'old con' is not a former prisoner but an ancient trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden horse the Greeks left at Troy was an ancient ruse, a confidence trick from antiquity.

clue.text: Attempt to conceal old misfortune

indicators.note: the attempt hides the other word inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
aged means old

explanation.surface: Trying to hide an old piece of bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a disastrous event, a great calamity or piece of bad luck.

clue.text: Instruments for blowers regularly seen

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of these words, at even intervals

explanation.surface: Wind instruments commonly seen being played by blowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are woodwind instruments, played by blowing through a double reed.

clue.text: A rotten crop — it is fruit

indicators.note: rotten means gone bad, so these letters decay into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bad harvest, and here is the fruit to prove it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Beginning to hail carriage, figure lifted headwear

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: air is carriage or bearing, the way one holds oneself

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifted means read upwards, so the figure's letters go in reverse

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: Someone hailing a horse-drawn carriage while a figure raises their hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' looks like a vehicle but means deportment, AIR; 'lifted' turns TEN into NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet is a fine mesh worn over the head to keep hair in place.

clue.text: Split by European uprising, group is recovering

indicators.note: the group is split open so that other letters are put inside it

parts.note: a ring is a group, as of conspirators
a coup is a revolt or seizure of power

explanation.surface: A political group, divided by a European revolt, is getting back on its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' looks like a reversal signal but simply means COUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to regain what was lost, so recouping is recovering it.

clue.text: Went in hospital ward before introduction to doctor

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A patient went into a hospital ward before meeting the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go into a place, so entered is went in.

clue.text: Din from Californian city doctor bitten by dog

indicators.note: being bitten by the dog means these letters sit between the dog's teeth, inside its letters

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
LA is Los Angeles
MO is Medical Officer

explanation.surface: A noisy scene in Los Angeles as a medic is savaged by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud, confused noise, the same racket as a din.

clue.text: Troop members caught that man on vessel with US characters

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
him refers to that man
a pan is a cooking vessel
Americans call the letter Z zee, so the plural characters are zees

explanation.surface: Soldiers caught a man on a ship along with some Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troop' reads as soldiers, but a troop is also a band of apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimpanzees live in groups called troops, so they are members of one.

clue.text: Uncovering line, refers to prompts

indicators.note: uncovering the word line strips off its outer letters, leaving only its inside

parts.note: to cite something is to refer to it

explanation.surface: Someone exposing a line of argument while pointing to sources.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite someone is to urge or spur them on, as prompts does as a verb.

clue.text: Do housework well with family coming round end of June

parts.note: a spring is a well, a source of water

indicators.note: the family comes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a clan is a family group

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Doing the chores thoroughly while relatives visit in late June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks part of the definition but is the start of the wordplay, SPRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring-cleaning is a thorough cleaning of the whole home, a big bout of household chores.

clue.text: Partners having issues with IT coming to the fore

indicators.note: coming to the fore says these two letters leave their place and go to the front of the word

parts.note: to issue something is to emit it
the clue's own two letters

explanation.surface: A couple whose problems involve information technology at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to the fore' takes IT from the end of EMITS and puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple romantically linked is called an item, so partners are items.

clue.text: Victor against odd disheartened soldiers

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: queer means odd or strange
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A winner facing down a strange band of dispirited troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the central E out of QUEER, leaving QUER.
explanation.definitionFit: A conqueror is one who wins a victory, so a victor.

clue.text: An empty potty gets deposit perhaps

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's potty with nothing in it gets something deposited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' looks like the toilet but means crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is one kind of payment, money handed over in advance, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Daughter tucked into more Brie after moving garnish

indicators.note: the daughter is tucked inside the other letters
moving the letters of more Brie puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A daughter tucks into extra cheese once she has moved the garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after moving' rearranges MORE BRIE, and D goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider is to embellish or decorate, which is what garnish means as a verb.

clue.text: Discontented tutor that is teacher assessed for suitability

indicators.note: with its contents removed only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An unhappy tutor, that is a university lecturer, being evaluated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' means emptied of contents, not unhappy: TUTOR loses its middle letters to leave TR.
explanation.definitionFit: To try on clothes is to put them on to see if they fit or suit.

clue.text: Special backing on board

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word on is read backwards

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Something remarkable being supported by a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable is worth noting, out of the ordinary and so special.

clue.text: Directed arm to fine area on animal's middle

parts.note: OK means fine

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A soldier pointed a gun at the midriff of a beast in a fine area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' is a weapon, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take aim is to point a weapon at a target, which is directing a firearm.

clue.text: Curse this writer audibly after upsetting experience

indicators.note: after puts the sound after the reversed word
in a down answer, upsetting turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to live through something is to experience it

indicators.note: audibly means as heard aloud, so the word for the writer becomes a sound-alike

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The setter, upset by an experience, utters a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reverses LIVE into EVIL; I said aloud is EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent look believed to put a curse on someone.

clue.text: Pure sample of orange lichen

indicators.note: sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A botanist taking a specimen of a brightly coloured lichen.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means like an angel, innocent and free of sin.

clue.text: Belgian city worker used to be contracted north of Portugal

indicators.note: in a down answer, north of means placed above, before the next piece

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: were is the past tense of be
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A worker who used to be on a contract above Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major port city in northern Belgium.

clue.text: Disreputable member of Parliament shackled by prison sentence

indicators.note: shackled means held in, so the member sits inside the sentence's letters

parts.note: life is a life sentence in prison
a parliament is the collective noun for owls, so one member is an owl

explanation.surface: A corrupt politician locked up for life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member of Parliament' looks like an MP, but a parliament is a group of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-life describes someone or something of disreputable, often criminal, character.

clue.text: Financial expert redistributed coins to me

indicators.note: coins being redistributed are shared out again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A money specialist hands some coins over to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist studies money and markets, an expert in finance.

clue.text: Around edges of woods deer look for water

indicators.note: the deer's letters go around the others, enclosing them

parts.note: a doe is a female deer

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Deer at the edge of a wood searching for something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' tells you the deer encloses the edge letters. Read 'look for water' as one verb phrase: it is the definition, not something the deer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to search for underground water with a divining rod.

clue.text: Woman getting an A with papers returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters for papers are read in reverse

parts.note: ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A woman gets top marks when her papers are handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is a woman's first name, as in the princess.

clue.text: Butcher's cut bearing wide bandage

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so this cut of meat holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: a saddle is a joint of meat, as in saddle of lamb
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide, a ball bowled out of reach

explanation.surface: A butcher with a large cut on him needs a broad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's cut' reads as a wound but is a joint of meat; 'bearing' looks like a compass direction but means carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: To swaddle is to wrap tightly in cloth, as one bandages a limb.

clue.text: Drink after retiring turned into delight

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the drink is read backwards

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer

indicators.note: turned means the letters of into are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone having a drink after retirement turns into a happy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after retiring' looks like leaving work but sends the drink backwards; 'turned' is the anagram signal for the word into, not a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great joy or happiness, a state of delight.

clue.text: Gathered across boat, fish caught for Billingsgate?

indicators.note: the gathered letters stretch across the boat, enclosing it

parts.note: met means gathered, as a meeting
the ark is Noah's boat

indicators.note: caught here means heard, picked up by the ear, so the fish's name is taken by sound

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Fishermen gathered on a boat with their catch bound for the London fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's famous fish market; the question mark marks it as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Billingsgate is an example of a market, a trading place for goods, here fish.
